target_customer: Home cooks and food enthusiasts buying a connected sous vide cooker, later meal kit subscribers
problem: Sous vide cooking was limited to restaurants and expensive lab style equipment; home cooks lacked an affordable, easy circulator.
business_model: Consumer hardware sales, later meal subscription (Nomiku Sous Chef meals, launched May 15, 2017)
product_category: Consumer kitchen hardware (sous vide immersion circulator)

founders.name: Lisa Q. Fetterman
education: NYU Arthur L. Carter Journalism Institute
founders.background_notes: Per Wikipedia: restaurant work and journalism; Forbes and Zagat 30 Under 30.

founders.name: Abe Fetterman
education: PhD plasma physics and astrophysics, Princeton

exit.reason: Company emailed customers that it was suspending operations; it said it could not reach a sustainable footing, a funding search near the end failed, and the market it created filled with competitors.

competitors.name: Anova
competitors.what: Consumer sous vide precision cooker from a lab equipment maker
competitors.traction_then: Entered consumer market within months of Nomiku's late 2013 launch, per review coverage

competitors.name: Sansaire
competitors.traction_then: Competed with Nomiku's $349 launch price from 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware design, heating control and connectivity manufactured in the US, which was hard for a small team but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Competitors from Sansaire and Anova appeared within months and cut prices, so the device was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals took the market; Joule was later acquired by Breville and Anova became a leader. Nomiku suspended operations in December 2019.

market_need_then: Home sous vide was growing: 2014 press called it a breakout year, and two Kickstarter campaigns raised over $1.3M in total.

branding.name_origin: Shortened form of the Japanese phrase Nomikui, meaning eating and drinking (per Wikipedia).

identity.visual_style: Designed consumer appliance; third co-founder Wipop Bam Suppipat was the industrial designer per Wikipedia

branding.brand_signature: The first clip on home sous vide circulator, born from Kickstarter
branding.community_and_virality: Two Kickstarter campaigns, a Shark Tank appearance, Inc. 30 Under 30 coverage in 2017 and celebrity chef users.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized pioneer in the category with strong press, but competitors with stronger products and prices overtook it.

pivots.to: Adding Sous Chef meal delivery subscription
pivots.why: To extend the product beyond the device; TechCrunch says awareness of the meals was hard to build.

outcome_analysis: Nomiku started in 2012 and raised over $1.3M across two Kickstarter campaigns, making sous vide affordable for homes. Rivals such as Anova, Sansaire and Joule entered, cutting prices, and the 2017 meal subscription pivot struggled for awareness. A late funding search failed and the company suspended operations on December 13, 2019. Its own success created the competitive market that took share.
